candidates.why: free_array_hdls(header_hdls) at 12851 frees the array and its items[].field/name strings, but the static global header_hdls (declared line 69) is never set to NULL. The error: label at 12862-12866 unconditionally calls free_array_hdls(header_hdls) again at 12864. If control ever reaches the error label after the normal-path frees (e.g. via a goto error from a later section, or any future reordering), this is a double free of the same pointer. The pointer is left dangling, so the second free at 12864 is a use of freed memory.

Same pattern: free_array_hdls(eed_hdls) at 12852 frees the array, but the static global eed_hdls (line 70) is not reset to NULL, and the error path frees it again at 12865. Dangling global pointer reused after free.

Same pattern: free_array_hdls(obj_hdls) at 12853 frees the array, but the static global obj_hdls (line 71) is not reset to NULL, and the error path frees it again at 12866. Dangling global pointer reused after free.

The three statics are freed at 12851-12853 (and 12864-12866) but never set to NULL. On a second call to dwg_read_dxf (e.g. dwg_read_dxfb at 12881 re-enters dwg_read_dxf), lines 12680-12682 overwrite them with new_array_hdls without freeing, and more importantly any path that reaches resolve_postponed_header_refs (12399-12400), resolve_postponed_object_refs (12450-12451) or resolve_postponed_eed_refs (12598-12599) after a free would dereference the freed array. The stale non-NULL globals make the freed memory reachable.

The CLASSES branch at 12739-12746 does 'return error' at 12745 instead of 'goto error', so it skips the frees at 12851-12853/12864-12866 and leaves the three statics pointing at live-but-orphaned arrays. A subsequent dwg_read_dxf call then reassigns them at 12680-12682, leaking; combined with the missing NULL reset this makes the ownership of the freed/leaked arrays ambiguous and the globals a stale-pointer hazard for the resolve_* functions.

free_array_hdls frees items[i].field (742) and items[i].name (743) but never NULLs them, and the loop bound hdls->nitems (740) is not reset. If free_array_hdls is called twice on the same array (which the 12851/12864 and 12852/12865 and 12853/12866 pairs allow), the second pass re-reads the freed items[] slots and frees the already-freed field/name pointers again — a double free of the strdup'd strings from array_push (720-721).

array_push reallocs hdls at 710 and, on failure, returns NULL at 715 without freeing the old block; the caller assigns the result back to the global (e.g. 1200, 1754, 9147, 11055), so the global becomes NULL while the old array is leaked. More relevant to use-after-free: the realloc result is stored into the caller's global, but any other pointer to the old array (e.g. a local alias) would be dangling after 710. Also note the realloc size at 711 uses '8 +' as a hardcoded header size rather than offsetof, so a size mismatch could corrupt the flexible array and make items[i].field/name at 720-721 write outside the allocation.
